Market design is a branch of economics that focuses on establishing rules of exchange, meaning who gets allocated what and by what procedure, in order to achieve efficient and equitable outcomes. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] It is closely related to mechanism design and auction theory . Market design is concerned with the workings of particular markets in order to fix them when they are broken or to build markets when they are missing. [ 4 ] Practical applications of market design theory, pioneered by scholars like Alvin Roth , have included labor market matching (e.g. the national residency match program), organ transplantation, school choice, and university admissions.
